newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP volatilities up as calls dominate.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP volatilities up as calls dominate.

text.p: Implied volatility of BTP options on LIFFE climbed on Thursday amid high turnover in out-of-the-money calls, options brokers said.
"We have moved up from about 6.7 percent (implied volatility) on the close last night to 7.2 percent at-the-money," said Mark Bays at Mees Pierson Derivatives.
"I think it is volatility bid up just on the size of the business. It is the positions that have gone higher rather than people thinking the market will be more volatile," Bays said.
Traders said a rosy view of Italy's bond market persisted, including lira strength and the country's prospects in the run-up to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
But any upset over the 1997 budget due on Friday could turn the tables on the market, brokers said.

"Everyone is feeling positive. How long it lasts we shall see," said Bays, an options broker. "No negative factors are being looked at all, which makes me feel slightly bearish, but I am prepared to go with it for the short-term."
Bays cited good call and call spread buying on Thursday.
He said investors were busy buying December calls in the 121.50/122.00 area against selling the 123.50/124.00 region, but there was practically no trade in puts.
By 1455 GMT, more than 7,200 lots of the 121.50/122.00 strikes were traded and 5,864 lots at the 123.50/124.00 strike. LIFFE screens showed not one trade in puts at any strike.
December BTP futures, buoyed by continued lira strength, hit a new record of 120.98 on Thursday before subsiding to 120.32 at 1455 GMT, still 37 basis points up on the day.
An options trader at an Italian bank said implied volatility should hold present levels for the rest of the week, but farther out the picture was less certain.
"In a sense we are on a cusp and the market could go either way," he said.
A satisfactory budget outcome would mean Italy's convergence process with other major European economies could continue, analysts said.
But if some crisis occurred or the budget were viewed as weak, the trader said "there might be some profit-taking since we have seen a big move without any kind of correction".
